_about: The scaling rules for every screen (decisions 24 and 25; rules F2, F4, F18). js/shared/frame.js reads this file, works out the form factor and one scale from the viewport, and writes every size token (--njg-*) on <html>; css/shared/tokens.css holds the same numbers as the first-paint fallback (build/test_shared_frame.mjs keeps the two equal). Change a number here and the next load uses it: nothing in CSS or code needs to change. All lengths are CSS px at scale 1 (a 1366x768 laptop).

formFactors._about: Landscape is assumed (a portrait phone gets the turn-your-phone card). short = the viewport's shorter side, aspect = long / short. First match wins: phone, then tablet, else laptop.

scale._about: One number per screen: scale = clamp(min, short / refShort, max). Every size token is its base value times this scale, then the floors.

floors._about: Never below these, whatever the scale (F2, F7: text 14 px, taps 48 px). Tokens listed under `textTokens` take the text floor, under `tapTokens` the tap floor; `unscaled` ones (hairlines) never scale. hand-w and hand-h are the onboarding's ghost hand, whose fingertip js/shared/onboard.js places in that box. Text that sits at the floor is set at 14.5 px (t4, flag-t, the phone's small sizes): half a pixel of room, so sub-pixel rounding never renders it under 14.

sizes._about: Base values (px at scale 1). `laptop` is the full set; `phone` and `tablet` list only what differs. t1-t4 are the design system's Nunito L1-L4 (CDS 2); side-* the sidebar's headline, row and sub-line; big-* the request pop-up; s1-s7 the 8-pt spacing; face the visible face on a card, face-hit its tap area; tool the guide box's bulb and mute; rail the nav dock's buttons; row-h and part-h an order card's item row and part; done the round Done tick. badge, end-* are the end screen's (js/shared/results.js): a badge's picture, its buttons, padding, the review's word, captions, the accuracy count, the buttons' words. end-card is the end screen card's widest, end-col a review column's widest.

sidebar._about: The sidebar's width (F4: about a fifth of the screen, on the left). width = clamp(min x scale, share x viewport width, max x scale); `fillAspect`: on a screen wider than that aspect the sidebar also takes the room the picture can't use (never past max).

stage._about: js/shared/stage.js: a scene is laid out in its own background pixels (1600x900, D15; a scene file may give its own size, e.g. the clinic's 1536x1024). itemScale: how much a play item may grow past the plain fit on this kind of screen, so a 4:3 tablet uses its height (the scene's sides past its safe area may go off screen to allow it). hiDpi: art at @2x is picked when devicePixelRatio x the drawn scale passes this.

scenes._about: A scene's own size and safe area (what must stay on screen), in its own pixels. `fill`: fit (the whole picture fits, Cook's Phaser EXPAND) or cover (the picture covers the play area, the clinic's rooms). anchorY: how a picture taller than the play area is cropped (0 keeps the top, 1 the bottom).

cook._about: Cook's stations: the shelf band's chips reach both edges of the design box (the chai tray's 'paani' chip starts near x 30), so the safe area is the whole box and a tablet shows the plain fit. To grow Cook's play items on a 4:3 tablet, R4 lays the stations out for it (a shelf that fits a narrower safe area, or two rows) and narrows this safe area; the stage then grows the scene up to stage.itemScale

clinic._about: each room's own `need` (data/clinic/scenes-v2.json) is its safe area across; its `ay` its anchorY

card._about: The order card's row layout per form factor (decision 25): `stack` = one row per line (today's); `pills` = short rows share a line as pills, wrapping, never clipped. Default stays `stack` until Zafar chooses.

rotate._about: The one turn-your-phone card (C2): shown when the screen is upright and narrower than this.
